summary.headline: Sheela Foam Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19% to INR1,045 crore, with operating EBITDA flat at INR87 crore (8.4% margin) as brand spend and raw-material inflation absorbed the gains.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY to INR1,045 crore, the first time quarterly revenue crossed INR1,000 crore. Operating EBITDA was INR87 crore (8.4% margin), flat YoY, while reported EBITDA was INR83 crore after a one-off INR7 crore provision against an Australian customer. PAT was INR46 crore versus INR10 crore last year, helped by operations, lower finance cost and depreciation. Management said raw-material inflation (polyol up 65%, TDI up 33% since mid-February) and a larger Great Sleepwell Festival spend compressed margins, and that absolute profit was held. Furlenco became a subsidiary from 1 October 2026 and will be consolidated line by line from Q3.

financial_highlights.value: INR781 crore, EBITDA INR61 crore (7.8% margin)
about INR10 crore per quarter (expected to continue)

segments.name: Mattress
segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew 11% with volumes broadly flat, reflecting price actions and festive-season shift; prices up about 25% since the Middle East conflict began.

segments.name: Foam
segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew 26% with volumes broadly flat; foam prices up about 35-40% since the conflict began.

segments.name: Australia (Joyce)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR241 crore, up 16% YoY, with EBITDA margin about 13.4%; Q2 margin 10.7% after a provision for a customer (A.H. Beard) in administration.

segments.name: Spain (Interplasp)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR250 crore, up 44% YoY, with EBITDA margin 10.7%; Q2 margin pressured by costs of winning new customers.

segments.name: Furlenco (subsidiary from 1 Oct 2026)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue about INR229 crore (up 34%), EBITDA INR89 crore (about 39% margin), subscribers up 35%; 200,000+ subscribers, 300+ products, 30+ cities; FY27 expected at about INR500 crore revenue.

segments.name: Staqo (IT/digital)
segments.commentary: Healthy EBITDA margin of around 28%, per management.

segments.name: U2O channel
segments.commentary: More than 10,000 touch points, growth about 41%; Q2 volume growth weaker after price increases vacated the INR8,000-9,000 price band.

guidance_outlook: Combined group (with Furlenco) targeted at about INR5,000 crore revenue and about INR600 crore EBITDA (margin a little above 12%) on a run-rate basis; standalone-plus-Furlenco FY27 split about INR4,300-4,400 crore plus INR500-600 crore.
Sheela Foam ex-Furlenco EBITDA margin: 9-10% currently; about 12% if pre-February conditions return; Furlenco adds about 3 percentage points.
FY28 EBITDA margin target of 13-15% now seen as difficult unless raw-material costs normalise.
Management intends 15% CAGR revenue growth irrespective of environment; volume-led if environment eases, value-led if not.

Net debt: existing Sheela Foam consolidated about INR600 crore currently, expected INR500-550 crore by year-end; with Furlenco (net debt about INR250 crore) total about INR800 crore. FY28 debt reduction about INR200 crore per annum from free cash flow of INR150-200 crore.
Gross margin unit economics designed for 42%+; current gross margin about 38%.
Furlenco listing may be proposed for next year; value unlock still under consideration.
capex_capacity: Furlenco accounted for as subsidiary from 1 October 2026: 43% fully diluted stake but about 35% held on converted-equity basis; line-by-line consolidation from Q3 with minority interest deducted.
Furlenco now buys its furniture assets (previously leased); manufactures about 20-30% in-house and outsources the rest; ROCE about 25%.
Sheela Foam is developing a support-layer technology to launch products below INR10,000 price point at mid-segment margins, and a new U2O product to refill vacated INR8,000-9,000 price band.
Sleepwell and Kurlon beds and recliners launched online via Furlenco back-end; store rollout to follow.
Australian and Spanish businesses onboarding new customers, with volumes expected from H2.
demand_pricing: Raw materials: crude up about 50%; polyol up 65% and TDI up 33% since mid-February 2026; prices rising INR10-20 every 15 days at peak.
Management passed on increases multiple times; mattress prices up about 25% and foam about 35-40% since the conflict began. Mattress entry price moved from under INR10,000 to INR11,000-12,000.
Festive season moved from late September (Q2) to October (Q3), shifting demand; management said market picked up in September and October.
Gross margin about 38% versus historical 40-42%; management estimated INR15-20 crore of EBITDA was forgone from the margin trade-off in Q2.
Management estimates about 15-20% of global TDI capacity wiped out (war and European closures), with polyol somewhat less; the main constraint is logistics rather than capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup and outlook of other income (INR22 crore over past two quarters)?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income includes returns on about INR110 crore of investments (10-12% p.a.) plus asset sale gains or revaluation items; expected to run at about INR10 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the INR5,000 crore revenue and INR600 crore EBITDA target?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a pro forma run-rate: existing Sheela Foam about INR4,300-4,400 crore revenue and INR400-450 crore EBITDA, plus Furlenco about INR500-600 crore revenue and INR200 crore EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q2 EBITDA margin compressed, and how much was marketing?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR15-16 crore extra advertising spend in Q2 versus plan; other expenses up INR8 crore YoY and INR15 crore QoQ; about INR8 crore of employee cost rise was FX translation of Australia and Spain, with yearly increments of 8-9%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 13-15% EBITDA margin target for next year still be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was on track before the war but is difficult now; achievable if raw-material costs normalise, with margin recovery of 2-3 points possible.

qa_highlights.question: Will volumes be reported by channel for the Sleepwell brand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split volumes by channel, saying it views the brand as omnichannel and looks at overall brand growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the Australian provision impact results?
qa_highlights.answer: A 38% haircut on receivables from A.H. Beard in administration cost about INR7 crore, booked across Q1 and Q2; management said it will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: Mattress volume outlook for H2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Depends on the Middle East situation; if raw-material costs stay high, management will keep protecting margins at the cost of some volume; if they flatten or soften, growth should follow.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidation accounting and minority interest after Furlenco became a subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidation is at the converted-equity share (about 35%) under accounting standards, moving to 100% line-by-line with minority interest deducted; fully diluted stake is about 43%.

qa_highlights.question: Debt outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR600 crore currently, expected INR500-550 crore by year-end excluding Furlenco; Furlenco net debt about INR250 crore; FY28 free cash flow of INR150-200 crore to reduce debt.

qa_highlights.question: Why are tax cash inflows showing INR33 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Amortisation of deferred tax assets from the Kurlon merger's tax-amortisable intangibles, plus a refund from revised returns for years after the October 2023 merger; management expects about INR150 crore of such benefit over one to two years.

risks_watch: Raw-material volatility: polyol, TDI and crude moves tied to Middle East disruption and Hormuz logistics; management said pricing relief depends on the Hormuz situation.
Margin trade-off: gross margin about 38% vs 40-42% historical; volume loss risk from repeated price hikes and consumer affordability limits.
U2O and sub-INR10,000 volumes: management is depending on new technology products to recover the vacated price band.
Furlenco consolidation and minority interest: complexity from 35% converted vs 43% diluted stake; listing and value-unlock timeline unclear.
Furlenco is capital-intensive (asset-based rental); management said net debt will not reduce there and it will draw cash to fund growth above 30%.
Australia (A.H. Beard) and Spain customer-acquisition costs weighed on Q2 margins; the Spain volume ramp is expected from H2.
key_quotes: With the strength of the brands, we've had the advantage of being able to pass these increases on to the market and eventually to the consumer.
So we had to provide those INR7 crores between the first and the second quarter.
If it prevails like this, I be lieve it's difficult to achieve, but if it normalizes, we will try to achieve it.
So we would suggest that we also look at it from the perspective of the overall brand and not through the channels from which it is sold.
But as far as payback or IRR is concerned, you understand that this is a competitive -- competition sensitive industry and those type of KPIs cannot be disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on brand strength, pricing power and the Furlenco turnaround, but cautious on margins: management openly said the margin target is difficult to hit while raw-material costs stay elevated. Evasive on channel-level Sleepwell volumes and on Furlenco IRR/payback, which it declined to disclose.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex amount or new plant announced; utilisation not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management openly said FY28 13-15% margin is difficult while raw-material costs (polyol +65%, TDI +33%) stay elevated; Q2 forgone EBITDA of INR15-20 crore and ~INR7 crore one-off provision.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Sub-INR10,000 support-layer technology product under development and new U2O product to refill INR8,000-9,000 band; Sleepwell/Kurlon beds and recliners already online with stores to follow.

rows.label: Net debt reduction to INR500-550 crore standalone by FY27 end
rows.why: Standalone consolidated net debt about INR600 crore now, guided to INR500-550 crore at year-end, with FY28 debt reduction about INR200 crore per year from FCF of INR150-200 crore; Furlenco net debt about INR250 crore keeps total near INR800 crore.

rows.label: Furlenco listing / value unlock
rows.why: Listing may be proposed next year, but value unlock is still under consideration and no timeline or IRR disclosed.

rows.label: Price increases and mix shift to INR11,000-12,000 entry price
rows.why: Mattress prices up about 25% and foam 35-40% since conflict began, with entry price moved from under INR10,000 to INR11,000-12,000; reversal depends on raw-material softening.
